notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mostly desert with little vegetation; flat in the middle and south, dry mountains on the north coast, greener mountains on the south coast.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Coverage is from a white pickup truck, mostly fully blurred, sometimes with just the antenna or front visible; lots of small desert tracks.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Private plates are generally yellow and commercial vehicles have red plates.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Arabic script with English often alongside, as in the neighbouring Gulf federation.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow edge lines with white middle lines; also common in the UAE, Israel and Jordan.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Black-and-yellow curbs are common.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Blocky, ornate light stone houses with a matching fence and often a fancier gate.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are blue with white text in two languages; the UAE and Qatar use similar ones.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Many signposts have black-and-white stripes; within the region only the UAE shares this.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles with several top designs; the one with a metal triangle above the wood is unique here, and poles are more common than in the UAE or Qatar.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Black-and-yellow chevrons with an unusually large number of arrows.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: High-voltage pylons painted red and white are common.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Garbage bins are black plastic or grey metal with a three-leaf logo and the text "be'ah".

notes.subject: car
notes.text: White taxis with orange side panels.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The north has dry mountains like the eastern UAE; the exclave in the far north is even drier and orange, with diagonal rock layers.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Around the southern coastal city of Salalah are rolling hills, bushes and some green valleys on a flat coastal plain.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Red sand dunes lie near the Saudi border and inland in the centre; orange-pink dunes with yellowish shrubs south of Bidiyah.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Umbrella-crowned acacias are common in the north; date palm plantations along the north coast; coconut palms near Salalah.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Gas pipelines beside roads and oil drills are common around Fahud and Amal.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Bin colour and stickers vary by governorate, e.g. black with black sticker in the north coast, grey with black sticker in Ad Dhahirah.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Masirah Island is dry and slightly hilly with grey soil, brown shrubs and a ring road with only a white centre line.
